name: Innsbruck
title: Holidays in Innsbruck
intro: An Alpine city where cable cars from the centre take you up into the snow, with Christmas markets below. Here's what Innsbruck is like with the family, when to go and how long to stay.
facts_note: The EU is bringing in new entry checks, so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: Mid-November to 6 January is Christmas market season, and the ski season starts in December. January to March has the most reliable snow. June to September is good for hiking and mountain lakes.

things.name: Old Town Christmas market
things.blurb: Stalls gather under the Golden Roof, with a giant crystal Christmas tree nearby.

things.name: Nordkette cable car
things.blurb: Funicular and cable cars rise from the city centre to over 2,000 metres in about 20 minutes.

things.name: Swarovski Crystal Worlds
things.blurb: A quirky park of crystal art rooms with a big indoor and outdoor play area, at Wattens nearby.

things.name: Alpine Zoo
things.blurb: Bears, wolves and ibex on a hillside above the city.

things.name: Skiing at Axamer Lizum and Glungezer
things.blurb: Several ski areas are within half an hour by free ski bus, and one ski pass covers them all.

things.name: Bergisel ski jump
things.blurb: Ride up to the top of the Olympic ski jump for a dizzying view.

faqs.question: Is Innsbruck good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes. You get a city with markets and museums plus snow and skiing within easy reach, all from one hotel.

faqs.question: When are the Christmas markets on?
faqs.answer: Usually from mid-November to 6 January, so you can still catch them after Christmas.

faqs.question: Is there snow at Christmas?
faqs.answer: Usually in the mountains above the city, though not always in town. Higher ski areas like the Stubai Glacier are the safest bet.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: A long weekend for the markets, or a week with skiing.
